data.title: FDA launches pilot program that aims to speed the time to first-in-human drug trials
data.description:
The US FDA is beginning a pilot program that aims to speed up the time from when a drug is first identified to beginning a first-in-human clinical trial to bring medicines to market more quickly.

Dubbed the Expedited Investigational New Drug ("IND") Pilot Program, the initiative involves having "drug companies [work] with qualified research institutions (QRI) that have scientific expertise to support efficient development of IND applications."

The FDA stated that in the US currently, first-in-human trials can take up to two years, considerably slower than in China and Australia, a reality that is "threatening America’s leadership in scientific innovation."

Research institutions chosen from the program will bring expertise to the IND process, "allowing the FDA to review and accept individual components on a rolling review during the pre-IND phase, rather than waiting for all components to begin review," the agency said. 

Applications are being accepted through Oct. 30, and the FDA expects to select eight to 10 sponsor-QRI pairs.

The program is one of the elements of HHS' Operation TrialBlazer, announced in June, that aims to have more clinical trials done domestically rather than oversees.

data.title: Energy shortages trigger new round of global market volatility - Nomura
data.description:
Global interest rates (BNDW) and cross-asset markets are waking up to an "energy / petrochem shock 2.0" as crude shortages become increasingly "terminal," according to Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott. Once again, crude oil (USO) (BNO) is proving to be "the straw that stirs the drink" of the current global macro risk regime, he wrote in a note published Tuesday.

Unlike the initial conflict phase during the Iran war, China is no longer depleting emergency stockpiles to ease supply tightness. Instead, McElligott noted, China is aggressively rebuilding crude inventories—"more than likely in coordinated conjunction with Iran to 'turn the screws' on the U.S." The result: crude prices pushing to new war highs, crunching cross-asset markets and pressuring already fragile equities sentiment while jacking up interest rate risk.

The macro fallout is spreading. Bonds (TLT) (TLH) (IEF), stocks (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ), gold (GLD), credit, and crypto (IBIT) are all "slowly bleeding out," while the U.S. dollar (DXY), energy equities (XLE), commodity carry, rates trend, and long volatility (VIXX) positions remain favored uncorrelated hiding places, McElligott said. Central banks face an impossible policy bind—stuck with what McElligott called the "useless 'demand-side' tool of 'policy rate hikes'" to sort out what is fundamentally a supply shock.

Meanwhile, tail risks are mounting. With U.S. President Donald Trump "backed into a corner of his own making," McElligott warned of a potential "left-tail bomb" on the global economy: a hypothetical U.S. energy export curb or ban that would devastate energy-dependent European and Asian economies.

Both Iran and China, he argued, are incentivized to keep the crisis simmering—and that scenario gains probability the longer the mess continues.

data.title: Rubrik reveals new coding harness built on Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 as AI concerns mount
data.description:
In the wake of growing concerns over increasingly capable artificial intelligence models and agents, Rubrik (RBRK) revealed Rubrik Code Guardian, a custom harness built on Anthropic's (ANTHRO) Claude Mythos 5.

"Frontier models are advancing at a fast pace. In the wrong hands, these models can be used to discover, chain, and exploit vulnerabilities at machine speed," said Rubrik co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Arvind Nithrakashyap. "To move just as fast, we are using frontier AI to scale vulnerability detection faster than our traditional code scanning tools. We took Anthropic's powerful model and built a Rubrik software harness to test on our code. We are using that experience and success now to give customers access to the harness, with a secure, isolated environment, which means we can run analysis of their code away from live repository and production systems."

The Rubrik Code Guardian embeds and harnesses Claude Mythos 5 into a service that operates directly on air-gapped copies of source code, enabling frontier model-level vulnerability analysis while minimizing risk and impact on production environments. It is currently available for select design partners in private preview.

In a separate announcement on Tuesday, the cybersecurity company introduced Rubrik MCP, or Model Context Protocol, which provides an organization's AI agents a secure, programmable path to Rubrik's data, identity, and application intelligence.

"We are seeing rapid growth with AI, and the addition of Rubrik MCP transforms security operations by seamlessly connecting customer AI agents directly into Rubrik's rich telemetry and governance framework," Nithrakashyap said. "Cyber threats accelerate at machine speed, and we are helping our customers use AI to maintain complete visibility and control across complex enterprise environments." 

Rubrik said one-third of its customers are currently utilizing Rubrik AI, which combines Anthropic's frontier models with Rubrik's domain expertise and security guardrails to deliver a multi-step reasoning agent engineered for critical incident response.

Rubrik's shares have nearly doubled in value over the past six months as cybersecurity concerns regarding AI have helped boost the stock. Last week, Wedbush initiated coverage of Rubrik with an Outperform rating and added it to its "Best Ideas" list.

data.title: GFL Environmental forms special committee to consider take-private - CTFN
data.description:
GFL Environmental (GFL) (GFL:CA) has created a special committee to consider a possible take-private. 

The special committee has retained a bank to advise on its review process, according to a CTFN report on Tuesday that cited a person familiar with the matter.

CTFN reported last month that bidders were said to have offered $50 to $55 a share for GFL, with bids due in the third week of September. The publication also reported in July that GFL (GFL)had had received offers from at least six private equity groups. 

Bloomberg also reported in July that GFL was considering a potential take-private transaction after drawing interest from buyout firms. CTFN reported in late July that GFL CEO/Chairman/Founder Patrick Dovigi was willing to consider a take-private offer of around $50 a share if he could roll over 100% of his stake.

Shares of GFL ticked lower by 0.6% on Tuesday.

data.title: Hornbeck Offshore wins North Sea decommissioning contract
data.description:
Hornbeck Offshore Services (HOS) gains 3.5% in Tuesday's trading after saying it secured a multi-year decommissioning contract with an unnamed "major operator" in the North Sea; financial terms were not disclosed.

The company said the contract for its Helix Well Ops subsidiary has an initial term of two years with extension options and begins in Q2 2027.

Under the contract, Hornbeck (HOS) will perform riserless plug-and-abandonment operations using either the Well Enhancer or Seawell well intervention vessels and deliver a fully integrated solution, including the vessel, a well-access system, ROVs, saturation diving, project management, and engineering services.

Helix Energy Solutions recently completed its combination with Hornbeck Offshore Services (HOS) after shareholders cleared the all-stock deal, creating an offshore services firm under the Hornbeck name.

data.title: Biggest stock movers Tuesday: Crypto stocks, PLAY, ENVA, and more
data.description:
Stock futures inched lower on Tuesday as Middle East supply risks, high bond yields, and calls for a deliberate pause in AI development weigh on sentiment ahead of the Fed rate decision.

Here are some of Tuesday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • Radiant Logistics (RLGT) +17% - Shares jumped after the logistics company reported strong FQ4 results with revenue rising 18.6% Y/Y. Adjusted net income increased 34.5% to $7.4M, while adjusted EBITDA rose 31.6% to $10.4M, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points to 15.5%. Gross profit increased 11.2% to $64.4M, with strength in U.S. forwarding operations and international airfreight. Radiant also amended its $200M revolving credit facility, extending maturity to 2031 and increasing its acquisition-focused accordion to $100M. The company entered fiscal 2027 with no net debt.

  • Waystar (WAY) +10% - Shares climbed following a report that the healthcare software provider is exploring strategic options, including a potential sale that could take the company private, roughly two years after its New York listing. Waystar has hired Evercore (EVR) to advise on the process, which remains at an early stage, according to the report. The company’s market value has fallen to roughly $4.8B after its shares declined 18% this year amid a broader software-sector selloff.

Biggest stock losers

  • Enova International (ENVA) -25% - Shares tumbled after the financial services company withdrew its applications with the OCC and Federal Reserve related to its proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp. Enova said the decision followed a thorough evaluation of the regulatory process, while CEO Steve Cunningham said the company did not believe regulatory guidelines provided clear standards for nonbanks seeking to become banks. The company reaffirmed its Q3 outlook for revenue growth of around 25% and adjusted EPS growth of around 30% Y/Y, along with FY2026 revenue growth of 20%-25% and adjusted EPS growth of 30%-35%. Enova also said it plans to accelerate share repurchases through the remainder of 2026, with $349M available under its current board authorization as of June 30.
  • Dave & Buster's Entertainment (PLAY) -15% - Shares plunged after higher food and beverage, payroll, and pre-opening costs pushed the entertainment and restaurant operator to an unexpected Q2 loss. Adjusted EPS came in at -$0.27, missing the $0.19 consensus and reversing from a $0.40 profit a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M from $129.8M and missed the $118.8M estimate. Revenue declined 2.4% Y/Y, as comparable-store sales weakened and entertainment revenue declined. Food and beverage costs rose 11%, entertainment costs 5%, and payroll costs 1%, pushing total operating expenses up 4%.
  • Circle Internet Group (CRCL) -8% - Cryptocurrency-linked stocks declined as fading legislative momentum for a comprehensive U.S. digital asset regulatory framework triggered broad selling across the sector. Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fell by 2.8%. Other decliners included BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR) -7%, Coinbase Global (COIN) -7%, Riot Platforms (RIOT) -4%, Marathon Digital (MARA) -3%, Strategy (MSTR) -5%, Robinhood Markets (HOOD) -3%, and HIVE Digital Technologies (HIVE) -3%.

  • Sysco (SYY) -3% - Shares fell after the foodservice distributor priced an offering of about 12.34M common shares at $81 each, with gross proceeds of roughly $1B. Sysco expects the offering to close September 16 and plans to use the net proceeds to finance part of the consideration for its pending acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot. Underwriters also have a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $150M of shares at the same price to cover potential overallotments.

data.title: Coca-Cola, Viking, and Aritzia are top consumer picks at UBS amid economic headwinds
data.description:
UBS named its top consumer discretionary stock picks even as the firm remained relatively cautious on spending due to subdued real wage growth, lower immigration, limited pricing power, tariffs, and low savings. "High operating leverage, accelerating GLP-1 adoption, and elevated price sensitivity add to the pressure, particularly for retailers and legacy department stores," warned UBS, although hotels were seen as a bright spot amid support from upper-income consumers. 

Coca-Cola Company (KO) is UBS' top pick across beverage, household, and personal care product names. "We believe KO has the ability to deliver +MSD organic revenue growth and +LDD underlying EPS growth, which compares to peers delivering +LSD revenue and EPS growth, standing out in a group where core growth is becoming scarce. While the stock trades at a low-30s premium vs. peers (vs. 5-yr historical premium of +LSD), we believe this premium relative to history is warranted given the degree of earnings visibility and upside," updated UBS.

In the fitness sector, Life Time Group (LTH) was the top pick, with UBS' price target of $57 implying ~37% upside. The near-term debate on LTH was noted to be on average member per center growth, and whether they can continue growing average center revenue per center membership and ultimately the impact on comparable center revenue.

Looking at food names, J.M. Smucker Co. (SJM) was tagged as the top pick. "In our view, SJM operates in categories that have demonstrated favorable growth characteristics relative to center-store packaged food over time. Specifically, we think that the company's top-line outlook could ultimately prove conservative as (1) management is still forecasting coffee volumes down LSD despite incoming deflation, and (2) segment momentum is improving across the board, with other portfolio brands delivering sequential improvement as we move through the year," highlighted the UBS analyst team.

As for leisure stocks, Viking (VIK) cruised in as the top pick. Viking (VIK) was called a pure play in luxury travel with a strong balance sheet. The view on VIK is that it has scarcity value for investors that look to invest in the luxury consumer, but specifically a consumer of luxury experiences rather than luxury goods.

Digging into SMID softlines, Aritzia (ATZAF) stood out to UBS. "We think ATZ's investments in differentiated store concepts, increasing relevance among consumers, and diversified product assortment should lead to sustained DD% sales growth. We expect the combination of robust comp sales, higher merchandise margins, and fixed cost leverage will drive a ~26% 5-yr. EPS CAGR," highlighted UBS.

data.title: Apple's "Widow's Bay" sweeps Emmys with 14 wins
data.description:
It was a big night for Apple (AAPL) at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards as its Widow’s Bay series swept the comedy category with 14 wins that included best comedy series, best actor, best supporting actress, and best writing and directing, as well as awards during last week’s Creative Arts Awards. 

The horror/comedy, which follows the exploits of Mayor Tom Loftis trying to boost tourism in his haunted New England town, set a record for the most Emmys won for a comedy series in a single season, beating The Studio’s (AAPL) 13 wins last year.  

Apple (AAPL) also walked away with trophies for its Pluribus and Slow Horses series. Nominated in 18 categories, Pluribus won awards for best actress in a drama and best writing, while 9-time nominee Slow Horses won for best directing for a drama series.   

Warner Bros. Discovery’s (WBD) HBO also came home with trophies for The Pitt (best drama and best actor), DTF St. Louis (best limited or anthology series), Task (best supporting actor), and Hacks, which ended its series run with 24 nominations but top honors only for Jean Smart as best actress in a comedy series.

In the late-night category, CBS’s (PSKY) Late Show with Stephen Colbert took home the trophy for best variety series, while Peacock’s Traitors (CMCSA) won for best reality competition program.

data.title: U.S. deficit-to-GDP contracted in government's FY26, Bessent says
data.description:
The U.S. deficit-to-GDP level declined to 5.7%-5.8% for the fiscal year 2026 from the “astounding level” of ~6.3% that the Trump administration inherited from the prior administration, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday.

"We would have continued that fiscal contraction this year but for the tariff refunds," he said during his testimony to the House of Representatives Financial Services Committee

"We will talk about a fiscal consolidation — that is coming," he added. 

Under President Donald Trump's second term, the private sector created more than 1M jobs, and real wages are outpacing inflation, he said in his prepared opening statement. However, CPI rose 3.4% Y/Y in August, but average hourly earnings increased 3.1% Y/Y in the same month, according to recent data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Bessent emphasized the administration's role in focusing international financial supervisory entities. During the G20 Finance Ministerial meetings earlier this month, economies representing more than two-thirds of global GDP agreed to address excessive and persistent imbalances, advance financial literacy, improve the global sovereign debt architecture, and support regulatory modernization. 

"In substance and in spirit, these priorities reflect the administration’s approach to international institutions by ensuring that American time and resources serve American interests," Bessent said. "We are also bringing that same discipline to the IMF and World Bank so they remain true to their core mandates and are better positioned to promote economic growth."

data.title: Russia, Ukraine launch overnight strikes on each other's oil infrastructure after Trump's claim
data.description:
Russia and Ukraine carried out aerial strikes on each other's energy infrastructure overnight Tuesday, despite President Trump's claim that both sides had agreed to stop hitting energy targets.

Ukraine ​hit the Syzran oil refinery in southern Russia and a drone production facility after Ukraine's President Zelensky said Russia "continues to attack our energy sector, regular logistics, and critical infrastructure," without elaborating; other officials said Russia had targeted gasoline stations in Kyiv and unspecified energy infrastructure in the southeastern Zaporizhzhia region.

Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was ready to halt such strikes but required credible guarantees from its partners that Russia would also ​stop, and a Kremlin spokesperson said Trump's suggestion was "a ⁠good initiative" but Western countries needed to lift sanctions against Russia and "unlawful restrictions on energy supplies."

Trump, under political pressure from rising fuel prices in the U.S., had said he told Zelenskyy that Ukraine needs to stop hitting diesel fuel in Russia.

The average price of a gallon of diesel in the U.S. hit a fresh record high of $6.27 on Tuesday, compared to $3.69/gal a year ago, according to the American Automobile Association.

Three of Russia's six top ​diesel-producing refineries were forced to significantly cut back or completely halt output in September due to ‌damage sustained in drone attacks, Reuters reported, citing calculations based on data from fuel market participants.

Crude oil futures continued to rise Tuesday as the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's critical East-West Pipeline and recent territorial gains by Houthi militants in Yemen have heightened worries over Middle East crude supplies.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery jumped 2.3% to $103.76/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery climbed 2% to $107.82/bbl.
